Import defaults remain 50 MiB and 512 entities; explicit integer max_source_mib:1..200 and max_entities:1..4096 may raise those requested budgets, while the 100000-face cap remains. Both import actions support preserve_labels:false to skip the optional second supplier STEP read for matching labels; default true preserves existing behavior. Source entity indices, source hash and native geometry remain retained; labels_status:not_requested explicitly reports absent recovered labels. Prefer summary:true for large imports: full validation still runs, but detailed object records are omitted; physical/reference names, counts, unit/source provenance and requested budgets remain, with a 512 KiB summary limit. Use paginated/scoped inspect afterward. Non-solid geometry is rejected by default. import_component/import_step may explicitly set preserve_reference_geometry:true to retain supported shells/faces as reference-only objects alongside solids; object_names lists physical solids and reference_object_names lists preserved surfaces. Reference surfaces have no mass/collision-solid claim; check geometry_coverage for omitted same-import surfaces. Native checkpoints preserve all geometry, but checked STEP save rejects any selection from a mixed import instance. render may explicitly include reference_objects:[names]; omission from rendering or physical checks must not be described as complete source coverage. Source history and PCB electrical connectivity are not imported; inspect returned object_names, place/check/save them. open_document: {path} opens an existing FCStd into an empty session; later checkpoints go to this run, preserving the source file. make_parameters: {name,parameters:{Gap:{value:12,min:1,max:30}}} creates shared dimensions in mm. Native Part::Mirroring also permits binding Base.x, Base.y, or Base.z plane-origin coordinates (not other object types); for example bind_parameter:{object_name:LiftRRMotor,parameter:Base.x,source_object:RearRotorLayout,source_parameter:RearMotorX,scale:0.5,offset_mm:52.5}. bind_parameter: {object_name,parameter,source_object,source_parameter,scale:1,offset_mm:0} binds a native editable dimension or Placement.Base.x/y/z to a shared dimension using a linear expression; then edit the shared source with set_parameter. boolean: {name,operation:cut|fuse|common,base,tool} creates a new native editable boolean from two distinct existing physical single solids; use a new result name. Empty/invalid results, no-effect cuts/fuses and disconnected fuses fail transactionally. Export final result only, not its construction operands. For a cut using an actual mating component, explicitly pass retain_tool_as_part:true; that mating tool may then be exported with the result only when their material does not overlap. mirror: {name,source,normal:[0,1,0],origin:[0,0,0]} creates a linked physical instance reflected across a plane; edit source dimensions to update both sides. Source and mirror may both be checked/exported; connectivity and collisions still require check. convert_spline_loft: {source,name,split_index,sampled_tolerance_mm} creates a separately named native spline loft from an existing solid ruled polygon-section Part::Loft without retyping coordinates. Source is preserved. Supports line-only Wright sections and copies supported shared-dimension section translation expressions; source coordinate edits are NOT associative. Records source geometry hash and snapshot provenance. Use explicit split and sampled tolerance, then inspect/check new outputs; not exact polygon equivalence or a certified continuous deviation bound. make_part: {spec:{name,kind,params}}; kinds box{x,y,z}, cylinder{radius,height}, tube{radius,bore_radius,height}, mount{x,y,z,bores:[[startXYZ,endXYZ,radius],...]}, loft{rings:[closed XYZ polygons]}, spline_loft{rings,split_index,sampled_tolerance_mm,ruled?:boolean} uses optional strict boolean ruled defaults true; false requests smooth native spanwise interpolation and requires renewed wall/interference checks (section sampled tolerance is not a 3D wall guarantee). Two interpolated native B-splines per closed section: 2-16 corresponding sections, 8-256 points per section, total <=2048, split leaves >=4 points on each branch, 0<tolerance<=1 mm. Tolerance measures sampled curve-to-source-polyline deviation, not a certified continuous bound. loft_shell{rings,inner}, extruded_skin{profile:[XYZ vertices],direction:XYZ,wall}, profile_plate{profile_object,direction:XYZ,thickness,bores} (links to an existing skin cavity profile). set_profile: {object_name,points:[XYZ vertices],summary:true} edits a constrained native sketch section, preserving spline type and provenance; inspect names first. set_profile and set_parameter summary:true keep full native validation/rollback but return compact edit metadata and dependent-name candidates; these are not contact checks. Scoped-inspect final physical outputs and run check after edits. Omit summary for legacy full document descriptions. set_parameter: {object_name,parameter,value,summary:true}; native properties Length/Width/Height or Radius/Height, extrusion LengthFwd, inward profile offset Value (negative), and supported Rocket tube Length/Thickness/AxialOffset (signed); only use names listed in editable_parameters. place: {object_name,position:[x,y,z],axis:[x,y,z],angle_degrees}; direct place is unavailable for assembly-controlled Rocket components. analyze_wing: {object_name,velocity_m_s:20,alphas_deg:[0,4,8],altitude_m:0,samples_per_branch:65,symmetric:true} runs the fixed open-source AeroSandbox/OptVL cross-check and separate NeuralFoil section polar analysis on actual current native two-branch spline-loft sections. Select a supported solid spline loft, often the outer construction loft, not a skin Boolean. Limits: velocity 1..100 m/s; 1..5 unique finite alphas in -10..12 degrees; altitude 0..20000 m; integer samples 33..129; strict boolean symmetric (right half-wing root must be at Y=0). Output directory is managed. Read-only: returns bounded numeric summary plus JSON/PNG/CSV artifacts, source geometry/runner hashes, mesh convergence and cross-solver comparison. Solvers approximate smooth spanwise CAD between sampled sections; symmetry is an assumption, and section polar confidence is not whole-wing stall proof. Do not claim full-aircraft stability, rotor-wash effects, structural integrity or flight readiness from this wing-only result. check_containment: {container:name,contents:[names],minimum_clearance_mm:0} measures actual solid containment and distance to all container boundary shells, allowing valid one-solid construction objects. Boundary distance is not clearance when contained:false; inspect per-object outside_volume/contained/clearance_passed and coverage. For wall clearance use the outer solid as container and cavity solid as content; for component fit use the cavity solid as container. It is read-only and does not prove load rating or manufacturing readiness. check_translation: {moving:[names],obstacles:[names],translation:[dx,dy,dz],samples:11} screens a straight removal/insertion path: clear only if conservative swept bounds prove no penetration, blocked if an actual sampled collision exists, otherwise inconclusive. It does not solve assembly joints or cable/tool access. check: {objects:[names],contacts:[[a,b],...],tolerance_mm:0.1,require_connected:true,summary:true}; summary computes all pairs but returns only clash and declared-contact pair details plus total counts/components; omitted pairs are not untested, and full evidence remains available in saved geometry-check.json. Omit summary or use false when every pair detail is needed. Prefer summary for large assemblies. Use require_connected for a single assembly; geometric connectivity is not a load-bearing joint verification. Declared contacts never exempt penetration. render: {objects:[final physical names],width:640,height:480,azimuth_degrees:35,elevation_degrees:25,deflection_mm:0.5,max_triangles:100000,angular_deflection_radians:0.35} uses optional angular_deflection_radians in 0.05..1.0. Render defaults remain max_objects:128 and max_source_faces:20000; explicit budgets may raise these to 4096 and 100000, but existing 100000-triangle and pixel/work caps still apply, so use scoped selections when full rendering fails. It returns a bounded native B-rep raster image with geometry fingerprint metadata; inspect the image together with native measurements, not as proof of fit or hidden geometry. save_preview: {objects:[physical names],reference_objects:[reference names],max_objects:512} writes an editable native document and GLB preview with explicit physical/reference counts and visible geometry_role metadata; it does not produce STEP or claim roundtrip_valid. The preview object budget defaults to 512 and may explicitly be set to an integer up to 4096. Include all intended reference objects and inspect preview_coverage for omissions. Use it to display mixed manufacturer geometry in the project without weakening checked export. save: {objects:[final physical output names]}; directory managed by the run. Native helper objects are not extra assembly parts. CAD edits do not automatically change the resolved domain design, flight checks or BOM; reconcile them explicitly. A passing CAD fit check is not manufacturing or flight approval.

args_json.description: Action parameters as a JSON object string; no Python code

tools.name: cad_action

tools.description: Design of experiments on the current design, read-only: for 1 to 3 design parameters, evaluate every check (including regression cases) at each point of a grid (or a Latin hypercube with 3 parameters or a grid over the point cap) and return a table with each point's passing count, failing checks and objective headlines, plus the Pareto front among the best points. Writes a CSV and an SVG plot under the run's sweeps/. Changes nothing: pick a point from the table and apply it with edit_design, then check. Bounded to 200 points and 20 s.

max_points.description: cap on evaluated points, 1-200; 60 is plenty for a first look

maximize.description: headline labels to maximize in the Pareto front; [] keeps the defaults (the domain objective, and each headline by its own bound)

minimize.description: headline labels to minimize in the Pareto front; [] keeps the defaults

params_json.description: JSON object string: design path -> range. A path is dotted ("envelope.balloon_g") or a JSON pointer ("/envelope/balloon_g"). A range is a list of values ([600, 800, 1200] or part ids) or {"min": 0.8, "max": 2.0, "steps": 7}. 1 to 3 paths, e.g. {"envelope.balloon_g": [600,800,1000], "envelope.fill_target_mps": {"min":4,"max":6,"steps":5}}

tools.name: sweep

tools.description: Hand one focused task to a specialist. It works on the shared DesignState with the same engineering tools and returns a short summary of what it changed and the numbers.

plan_task.description: id of the plan task this delegation does (required once a plan is set; "" before one)

task.description: the task, with the failing check names and margins it should fix

tools.name: delegate

tools.description: Write (or rewrite) the engineering plan: a DAG of tasks from requirements through sizing, structures, electronics/avionics, sourcing and fabrication to review. Each task names its owner, the tasks it needs first and the checks it must turn green. Rewriting keeps the status of tasks whose id, inputs and checks are unchanged. Rejected for an unknown owner, input or check, or a cycle.

goal.description: one line: what the finished vehicle must be

checks.description: declared checks this task must turn green; [] if none measures it

inputs.description: ids of the tasks whose results this one needs; [] for none

owner.description: who does it: you (orchestrator), a specialist role, or the reviewer

title.description: what the task produces, one line

tools.name: plan_set

tools.description: Move one plan task: pending, running, done or blocked, with a note. done is refused while any check the task names is failing or any input is unfinished. Tasks you delegate are moved by the harness; use this for your own tasks and to unblock or re-queue.

note.description: one line: the result, or why it is blocked

tools.name: plan_update

tools.description: End this round and send the design to the hostile reviewer. Call it when every check passes, or when you cannot make more progress this round.

summary.description: what the design is and what changed this round, with key numbers

tools.name: submit

tools.description: Run one post-design analysis on the current design (it is built first): CFD, FEA, a flight sim, fabrication, CAD. Returns the stage's own checks and numbers; a failing stage check is evidence to act on (e.g. an FEA hot spot: delegate a structures fix, then check). Slow: run it when the declared checks pass, not every turn.
tools.name: run_stage
